title: JWT authentication in the middleware pipeline
summary: Register JWT bearer authentication, order the pipeline, and protect an action with a role requirement.

scenario.briefing: The catalog action is open to anonymous callers because the application never registers an authentication scheme and never runs the authentication middleware. Add JWT bearer authentication and protect the action.

objectives.description: Register JWT bearer authentication and authorization services.
Require an authenticated member on a controller action.
Distinguish a missing identity from a missing role.

hints: AddAuthentication selects the default scheme; AddJwtBearer configures it.
Read the authority and audience from configuration.
Put [Authorize(Roles = "Member")] on the action that reads the catalog.

misconceptions.description: Registering authentication without adding it to the pipeline.
misconceptions.testDescription: Authentication runs before authorization and endpoint mapping.
misconceptions.feedback: The service registration creates the handler. UseAuthentication must run so the handler populates HttpContext.User.

misconceptions.testDescription: Authentication runs before authorization and endpoint mapping.
misconceptions.feedback: Authorization reads the identity established by authentication. Reverse the order and every caller looks anonymous.

misconceptions.description: Relying on the controller route to imply authentication.
misconceptions.testDescription: The catalog action requires an authenticated member.
misconceptions.feedback: A route is only a path. Add [Authorize] with the role requirement; otherwise the action is anonymous.

misconceptions.description: Returning 401 for an authenticated caller without the role.
misconceptions.feedback: The identity is known, so the correct response is 403. A 401 challenges a caller who has not authenticated.

sections.title: Authentication fills the identity
sections.body: AddAuthentication registers the default scheme and AddJwtBearer configures token validation against an authority and audience. UseAuthentication runs the handler and sets HttpContext.User. Without the middleware, the identity stays empty even though the service is registered.

sections.title: Authorization consumes the identity
sections.body: UseAuthorization evaluates policies and attributes such as [Authorize(Roles = "Member")]. It must run after authentication because it reads the user that authentication produced. MapControllers adds the endpoints that the pipeline protects.

sections.title: 401 and 403 are different answers
sections.body: 401 means the caller has not authenticated. 403 means the caller is authenticated but lacks permission. A role requirement turns an authenticated non-member into 403, not 401.

vocabulary.definition: A named handler that validates credentials and creates an identity.
An authorization header scheme that carries a signed token.
A rule that decides whether an identity may use a resource.
The registration order that determines which components process a request.

steps.title: Register the authentication pipeline
steps.prompt: Edit Program.cs. Register JWT bearer authentication with the authority and audience from configuration, add authorization, and place the middleware in a safe order.
hints: AddJwtBearer receives an options callback for Authority and Audience.
UseAuthentication must come before UseAuthorization and MapControllers.

localVerification.description: Build the host and run the authentication pipeline tests.

tests.description: JWT bearer authentication uses configuration for its authority and audience.
Authentication runs before authorization and endpoint mapping.

steps.title: Protect the catalog action
steps.prompt: Edit CatalogController.cs. Require an authenticated member for the list action while keeping the API controller and route.
hints: Place [Authorize] on the action that reads the catalog.
Add Roles = "Member" so a bare authenticated user is not enough.

tests.description: The catalog action requires an authenticated member.
The controller remains an API controller with its route.

steps.title: Transfer to an authenticated non-member
steps.prompt: A user authenticates successfully but has no Member role. The list action requires [Authorize(Roles = "Member")]. Which response is correct?
hints: The caller is authenticated; the token was accepted.
Authorization checks the role after authentication.
401 is for a missing or invalid identity.
403 is for a known identity without permission.

quiz.prompt: A user authenticates successfully but has no Member role. The list action requires [Authorize(Roles = "Member")]. Which response is correct?

options.label: 403 because the identity is known but lacks the required role.
401 because the caller lacks the Member role.
200 because any authenticated user may read the catalog.
302 to the login page because the role is missing.

quiz.explanation: Authentication succeeded, so the server knows the caller. Authorization then rejects the missing role with 403. A 401 would incorrectly suggest that the caller never authenticated.
